_note: SF neighborhood content, districts 5-7. See d1-d4.json for the sourcing rule.

neighborhoods.name: Noe Valley
neighborhoods.intro: Noe Valley is the district's family centre — sunnier and flatter than the hills around it, built around the 24th Street corridor of independent shops and cafes. The stock is largely Victorian and Edwardian on a regular grid, and it is one of the highest-volume single-family markets in San Francisco.
near: A walkable corridor of independent retail and cafes
Muni Metro along Church Street to downtown

neighborhoods.name: Eureka Valley & Dolores Heights
neighborhoods.intro: Eureka Valley is the Castro and the streets around it; Dolores Heights is the steep view ground rising to its east. Together they form the district's most recognisable address, with large Victorians on hillside lots and one of the busiest commercial strips in the city.
near: The city's best-known park, on the eastern slope

neighborhoods.name: Cole Valley & Parnassus Heights
neighborhoods.intro: Cole Valley is a compact, village-scaled pocket below Mount Sutro, with a short retail strip at Cole and Carl and Edwardian homes on the surrounding blocks. Parnassus Heights climbs above it toward the UCSF campus.
near: A small, well-used neighbourhood retail corner

neighborhoods.name: Glen Park
neighborhoods.intro: Glen Park sits at the district's southern edge with its own BART station and a small village centre at Diamond and Chenery. Glen Canyon Park gives it something no other city neighbourhood has — genuinely wild open space at its back.
near: A wild canyon with trails and a creek
BART and Muni at the village centre

neighborhoods.name: Haight Ashbury
neighborhoods.intro: Haight Ashbury runs along the south side of the Panhandle, with some of the largest intact Victorians in the city. Detached single-family sales are uncommon here — most of the stock is flats and multi-unit buildings.
near: The park and Panhandle at the northern edge
Metro to the south, frequent buses on Haight

neighborhoods.name: Duboce Triangle
neighborhoods.intro: Duboce Triangle is a dense, transit-rich wedge of Victorian blocks between the Castro and the Lower Haight. Almost everything here is flats and condominiums — detached single-family homes essentially do not trade.
near: A neighbourhood green at the centre
Muni Metro and the N-Judah surface line

neighborhoods.name: Corona Heights
neighborhoods.intro: Corona Heights climbs the rocky outcrop above the Castro, and the elevation is what defines it — view lots on steep streets, with the bare red summit as the neighbourhood's landmark.
near: A rocky summit with wide views across the city
A children's museum at the foot of the park
Muni Metro a short walk south

neighborhoods.name: Mission Dolores
neighborhoods.intro: Mission Dolores covers the flat blocks around the park and the mission the district takes its name from. The stock is overwhelmingly flats and condominiums rather than detached houses.
near: The city's best-known park, with the skyline view
The oldest surviving building in the city
BART and Muni within a short walk

neighborhoods.name: Twin Peaks
neighborhoods.intro: Twin Peaks is the district's high ground — quiet, fog-prone and carrying the widest views in San Francisco. Homes here are spread along winding streets below the summit.
near: Grassland and rare habitat on the slopes
Muni Metro down the western slope

neighborhoods.name: Clarendon Heights
neighborhoods.intro: Clarendon Heights sits on the ridge below Sutro Tower, a small pocket of large homes with long views east. Very few properties trade here in any quarter.
near: A rocky outcrop with panoramic views east
N-Judah down the hill to the north

neighborhoods.name: Buena Vista
neighborhoods.intro: Buena Vista wraps the city's oldest park, with large Victorians and Edwardians on the steep streets around it. It sits between Haight Ashbury and the Castro, sharing the character of both.
near: The city's oldest park, wooded and steep

neighborhoods.name: Hayes Valley
neighborhoods.intro: Hayes Valley is the district's retail and restaurant centre, dense and highly walkable since the freeway that once cut through it came down. Detached single-family homes are rare — the market here is flats and condominiums.
near: A dense corridor of independent shops and restaurants
Symphony, opera and ballet a few blocks east
Multiple Muni Metro lines and BART nearby

neighborhoods.name: Alamo Square
neighborhoods.intro: Alamo Square is built around the hilltop park and its row of Painted Ladies, with some of the largest and most intact Victorians in the city on the surrounding blocks. It is the district's grandest stock.
near: A hilltop green with the Painted Ladies view
Frequent bus service across the city

neighborhoods.name: North Panhandle
neighborhoods.intro: The North Panhandle — NoPa — is a consistent grid of Edwardian blocks just north of the Panhandle strip. It is dense, walkable, and largely a flats-and-condominium market rather than detached houses.
near: A green strip running east from Golden Gate Park

neighborhoods.name: Western Addition
neighborhoods.intro: The Western Addition is a broad, mixed neighbourhood at the district's core, with Victorian blocks alongside mid-century redevelopment. Its market is overwhelmingly condominiums and apartments.
near: One of three remaining Japantowns in the country

neighborhoods.name: Anza Vista
neighborhoods.intro: Anza Vista is a small post-war pocket on the hill near the Kaiser medical centre, more suburban in form than the Victorian blocks around it. Very little trades here in any quarter.
near: Hilltop parkland a short distance south
Everyday retail along the northern edge

neighborhoods.name: Lower Pacific Heights
neighborhoods.intro: Lower Pacific Heights covers the blocks below California Street, sharing the architecture of the crest above but at more attainable prices. Fillmore Street runs through its centre.
near: One of the city's most established retail corridors
Frequent bus service across the city

neighborhoods.name: Panhandle
neighborhoods.intro: The Panhandle is the narrow green strip running east from Golden Gate Park, with dense Edwardian blocks along both sides. The market here is flats and condominiums rather than detached homes.
near: A tree-lined green strip with paths and playgrounds

neighborhoods.name: Pacific Heights
neighborhoods.intro: Pacific Heights runs along the crest above the northern waterfront and is the most expensive residential ground in San Francisco. The largest houses sit on the north-facing blocks where the Golden Gate views are, with Fillmore Street carrying the retail below.
near: Golden Gate and bay views from the northern blocks
An established corridor of shops and restaurants
Two hilltop parks within the neighbourhood

neighborhoods.name: Presidio Heights
neighborhoods.intro: Presidio Heights sits west of Pacific Heights along the Presidio's southern wall, with large homes on quiet streets and Sacramento Street as its retail spine. It is among the most consistently expensive addresses in the city.
near: Boutiques and galleries along the corridor

neighborhoods.name: Marina District
neighborhoods.intro: The Marina occupies the flat, filled ground along the northern waterfront, with Marina-style flats and homes on a regular grid. Chestnut Street carries the retail and the bay is a block away from much of it.
near: Waterfront lawns and a bay-side promenade
A busy corridor of shops and restaurants
The 1915 rotunda at the western edge

neighborhoods.name: Cow Hollow
neighborhoods.intro: Cow Hollow sits on the slope between the Marina and Pacific Heights, anchored by Union Street's shops and restaurants. The stock is a mix of Victorians, Edwardians and flats, on ground that rises steadily south.
near: A long-established retail and restaurant corridor

neighborhoods.name: Presidio
neighborhoods.intro: The Presidio is the former army post at the city's northwest corner, now national parkland with a limited stock of leased and privately held housing. Almost nothing trades here on the open market.
near: 1,500 acres of forest, trails and bay overlooks
Waterfront promenade and a Pacific beach
